claim: Every condition the simulation can put on a person or a piece of property is classified by the renderer and draws a clip the library actually holds.

defectFound.summary: public/motion.js bound the injured pose to conditions the simulation has never set.

whatTheSimActuallySets.note: 'minor-injury' is set in sim/directors.mjs and cleared by advanceRoutine once recoversAt passes. Neither 'injured' nor 'wounded' appears anywhere in sim/.

defectFound.consequence: A hurt person fell through the condition branch entirely and was drawn by task instead - rust-rest for somebody the director had put at rest, or an idle pose. The delivered injured-rest art sat behind a binding that matched nothing, which is the same class of fault the binding was originally written to fix.
defectFound.whyTheOldTestMissedIt: tests/motion-binding.test.mjs asserted the pose for 'injured' and 'wounded' - the same two invented names the implementation used. The test and the code agreed with each other and neither agreed with the simulation. Restating a vocabulary in a second place is what allowed the drift.

fix.motion: public/motion.js now exports HURT_CONDITIONS ('minor-injury', 'injured', 'wounded'), STILL_CONDITIONS ('dead', 'captured') and ORDINARY_CONDITIONS ('well', 'tired'), and the branches read those lists. 'injured' and 'wounded' are retained as accepted names so a future server state does not silently fall through.
fix.guard: tests/motion-binding.test.mjs no longer restates the vocabulary. It scans sim/*.mjs for condition literals, adds anything reachable through marchCost(), and requires every one to be classified and to resolve to a clip present in animation.json. A condition added to sim/ without a binding now fails with a message naming the list to add it to.
fix.collision: An ox and a wagon carry a `condition` too, and entityClip reads `entity.health?.condition || entity.condition`, so the two vocabularies share one code path. The test asserts no property condition appears in HURT_CONDITIONS or STILL_CONDITIONS - a wagon whose condition was ever named 'wounded' would otherwise be drawn as a hurt person.

discoveredByTheGuard: The scan immediately surfaced 'lost', which is a wagon condition rather than a person's. That is why the property vocabulary is now handled explicitly instead of being swept in with the rest.

browserProof.method: Live five-household class, real browser student as hh-1, class paused so no incoming snapshot could overwrite the projection under test. The renderer's own `window.__animationClips` set was used, which records a clip only when `animated()` actually drew it with a non-zero width - so this measures pixels, not intent. The same person and the same task were drawn twice, changing only the condition in the received projection.
browserProof.visual: Thomas drawn hunched at rest beside the cabin, with the selection panel reading 'rest · Family 1 home · minor-injury'.
browserProof.whyTheProjectionWasConstructed: The condition was written into the received projection rather than played into existence, because it cannot currently be played into existence - see the limitation below. The defect was entirely in the renderer's reading of a projection, so a constructed projection is the right level to prove it at, but it is not a played outcome and is not recorded as one.
browserProof.falseStart: A first attempt read no injured clip. The class was still running and a new snapshot arrived every 1200 ms, overwriting the mutation before the redraw. Pausing fixed it. A second attempt read nothing at all: while paused the animation loop does not redraw, so the draw had to be forced with a real viewport change. Both were measurement artefacts, not product faults, and are recorded because either could be mistaken for one.

limitation.minorInjuryIsUnreachableInPlay: Measured across three full classes with every household helping and marching upriver, the only conditions any person ever held were 'well' and 'tired'. Nothing makes a person tired before settleHelp, which is the same moment the march cost is applied, so every marcher is 'well' when it lands. 'minor-injury' therefore never occurs in a played slice today, and the risk text a student reads is always 'will come back tired'.
limitation.keptAnyway: State is preserved between arcs, so somebody who ends this slice tired starts the next one tired, and a fatigue system is already on the roadmap. The rung is marked with a ceiling: note in sim/directors.mjs.
limitation.correction: An earlier note in docs/evidence/upriver-march.json said the upriver work made 'minor-injury' reachable in ordinary play for the first time. That was wrong and has been corrected in that file.

notProved: That a student will ever see this pose in a normal lesson. They will not, until fatigue has another source.
